issues.description: Class: SealSaloon. The problem statement (UML and text) requires a public constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts a saloon name and instructs initializing attributes (orders and final Stock) in the constructor. The solution implements only a no-argument constructor public SealSaloon() and does not accept or store a name. Additionally, the problem text elsewhere requires the stock attribute to be static and some initialization guidance implies instance-constructor initialization of stock, creating a contradictory expectation: the spec asks for an instance constructor SealSaloon(String) and to initialize attributes there, while also mandating a static stock shared across instances. This mismatch makes it unclear which constructor signature students must implement and how the shared static stock should be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and implementation consistent. Preferred resolution: Update the solution to add a constructor public SealSaloon(String name) that stores the provided name in a private field (with a getter) and initializes instance attributes such as orders there. Keep the stock attribute static but initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). Alternatively, if you want a no-arg constructor, revise the problem statement to specify a no-argument SealSaloon() and clarify that the static stock is initialized at declaration or in a static initializer rather than in an instance constructor.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for the SealSaloon class: the problem statement (UML and text) requires a constructor SealSaloon(String) that accepts the saloon name, but the provided artifacts use a no-argument constructor SealSaloon(). Specifically, the problem statement lists +SealSaloon(String) and says "The constructor takes the saloon name as a String parameter", whereas the template example in Main.java constructs SealSaloon with no arguments and the solution implementation (SealSaloon.java) defines public SealSaloon(). This inconsistency leaves students unclear whether to implement a constructor that accepts a String and where to store the name (and whether a getter is expected).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor signature consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement to require a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() (and remove references to a name parameter), or (B) Change SealSaloon.java to provide public SealSaloon(String name), add a private final String name field and a public getter getName(), and update the example usage in Main.java (and any tests) to pass a name when constructing SealSaloon. Ensure the chosen approach is documented in the problem text so students know which constructor to implement.
